title: Augmented Difference-in-Differences
eligible_reason: Methods paper proposing the augmented DiD (ADID) estimator, a single-treated-unit counterfactual method in the synthetic-control family: regress the treated unit's pre-period outcome on an intercept and the cross-sectional average of the control units, then predict the post-period counterfactual. All three empirical applications have one treated unit (or one treated product group) and one treatment date: a Boston showroom opening (83 pre-treatment weeks, 10 control units, simulated data), California after the Nov 8, 2016 recreational marijuana legalization (40 pre / 30 post weeks, other states as controls), and a Brazilian retailer's price change on one product (T0 = 249, data from Fan, Masini and Medeiros 2022). No panel TWFE regression exists in the code and there is no staggered adoption, so the two-adoption-date rule fails.
design_notes: MATLAB scripts compute, for each application, (i) a 'DID' ATT = mean over post periods of y_treated minus (pre-period intercept + control-unit average), and (ii) the ADID ATT from a pre-period OLS of y_treated on [1, mean of controls] with an asymptotic standard error; both are single-time-series comparisons, not regressions with unit and time fixed effects. ADID_showroom.m: t = 110 weeks, t1 = 83, one treated series, 10 controls (Showroom_Generate_Data_Boston.csv, simulated). ADID_marijuana_cigarettes.m: weekly cigarette revenue panel 2014-2019 from Kilts Nielsen scanner data, treatment week 158 (Nov 8, 2016) for California (column 5), control states in columns 9+. ADID_Brazil_Price_Change.m: loads data_product_1..5 (not shipped), treated products' sales vs control products' sales around a price change at T0 = 249. The full-text 'staggered' hit presumably comes from the methods discussion.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One treatment date per application (Boston showroom opening; Nov 8, 2016 legalization for California; one price change for the Brazilian product).

data_files_note: Only the showroom application ships data, and the README calls it 'Simulated data'. The cigarette panel must be rebuilt from Kilts Nielsen scanner data (licensed) with the shipped R script; the Brazilian retailer data must be downloaded from Fan, Masini and Medeiros (2022, JASA).
software_notes: MATLAB for all DID/ADID estimation and figures; one R script (readr, dplyr, data.table) to build the cigarette revenue panel from Kilts Nielsen files.
priority_note: Not eligible: single treated unit and single date in every application; estimator is not a TWFE regression.
